Real output also depends on fuel moisture: wood at 45 pc carries roughly half the usable energy of wood at 20 pc, and that is a property of the FUEL, not the stove.

coefficients.condition: As for a wood stove: from the legal minimum (65%) to a 7-star appliance, and about half the heat from damp wood.
coefficients.condition_fr: Comme un poêle : du minimum légal (65 %) à un appareil 7 étoiles, et environ moitié moins de chaleur avec du bois humide.
coefficients.source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2015/1185 (ecodesign, solid fuel local space heaters)
coefficients.notes: Same regulatory basis as the wood stove; cookers are named separately in Annex II. MOVED TO COOKING HEAT 2026-09-04. This is a COOKSTOVE and its delivered figure now lands where cooking is measured. How much of that heat reaches the pot rather than the room is not in the source, so its space-heating contribution stays unmodelled rather than being invented. DEMOTED TO REFERENCE 2026-09-05, when the cooking demand was written. This figure is fuel to HEAT DELIVERED BY THE APPLIANCE; IO-44's demand is heat delivered INTO THE PAN. A cookstove's body radiates into the kitchen as well as into the pot, and no source here splits the two, so summing this against a pot-delivered demand would compare two different quantities and would do it optimistically. Kept as a recorded reference figure rather than deleted: the stove efficiency is real and sourced, it is simply not the quantity this family measures. | Condition as first written: SEASONAL space heating energy efficiency as the regulation defines it, which carries corrections for controls and is not a bench figure. 0.65 is the floor to be placed on the EU market since 1 January 2022; a pellet appliance must reach 0.79. The upper end here is Flamme Verte 7-star territory and is NOT separately sourced. Real output also depends on fuel moisture: wood at 45 pc carries roughly half the usable energy of wood at 20 pc, and that is a property of the FUEL, not the stove. The regulation sets the same 0.65 floor for cookers.

coefficients.condition: Biogas from each kilogram of kitchen scraps, worked out from the published figures for the part that digests. A cold digester in a Normandy winter makes less.
coefficients.condition_fr: Le biogaz tiré de chaque kilo d’épluchures, calculé à partir des chiffres publiés pour la part qui se digère. Un digesteur froid, l’hiver en Normandie, en produit moins.
coefficients.source: Peer-reviewed anaerobic digestion literature for the yield, and food-waste characterisation studies for the solids fractions
coefficients.notes: The per-kg-VS figure is recorded separately as a reference row so the derivation is visible rather than buried in this condition string. | Condition as first written: DERIVED, and the derivation is the honest part: 0.55-0.75 m3 biogas per kg VOLATILE SOLIDS (peer-reviewed) x 0.136-0.238 kg VS per kg of wet food waste (16-25 pc total solids, of which 85-95 pc volatile). A 2.4x span, hence P3. Mesophilic digestion of household food waste; a cold digester in a Normandy winter will sit below this.

coefficients.condition: The published figure, per kilogram of the part of the waste that digests, not per kilogram of wet scraps (four to six times less).
coefficients.condition_fr: Le chiffre publié, par kilo de la part des déchets qui se digère, et non par kilo d’épluchures humides (quatre à six fois moins).
coefficients.source: Peer-reviewed anaerobic digestion literature on food-waste digestion
coefficients.notes: RECORDED, NOT SUMMED: nobody can weigh their volatile solids. It is here so the derivation behind the active per-kg-wet row is visible and checkable, which is the whole point of keeping figures we do not calculate with. | Condition as first written: The primary literature value, stated per kg of VOLATILE SOLIDS as published. Not per kg of wet waste, which is 4-6x different and is the single easiest denominator in this catalogue to get wrong.

coefficients.condition: Drinking water made for each litre drawn from the tap. An ordinary under-sink unit sends three to four litres down the drain for each litre it makes.
coefficients.condition_fr: L’eau potable produite pour chaque litre tiré du robinet. Un appareil sous évier ordinaire envoie trois à quatre litres à l’égout pour chaque litre produit.
coefficients.source: Water Quality Association RO fact sheet and water-treatment industry sources
coefficients.notes: The decision-relevant fact about reverse osmosis for this catalogue's audience, and the one a product page is least likely to lead with. | Condition as first written: RECOVERY: litres of drinking water produced per litre drawn from the tap. A standard under-sink unit runs 20-25 pc, meaning THREE TO FOUR LITRES GO TO THE DRAIN for every litre produced. Permeate-pump models reach about 50 pc. Higher recovery buys less waste at the cost of permeate quality.

coefficients.condition: Per candle, filled from above. It slows as the top chamber empties, so this is the fastest it goes.
coefficients.condition_fr: Par bougie, remplie par le haut. Le débit baisse quand la chambre du haut se vide : c’est donc son maximum.
coefficients.source: Doulton ceramic candle documentation and gravity-filter operating guidance
coefficients.notes: Sits alongside the bio-sand filter's 12-24 L/h so the two household treatment options are directly comparable, which is the decision a reader actually faces. The ceiling is high enough that it will rarely bind. | Condition as first written: PER CANDLE, gravity-fed. 1-3 L/min is the rated range and the manufacturer recommends restricting to about 1.5 L/min for filtration performance; the rate falls as the upper chamber empties, so this is a ceiling and not a sustained output. A PRESSURISED multi-candle module is a different device entirely, at up to 2,000 L/h.

coefficients.condition: The chamber's volume per person, counting the sawdust or wood shavings added each time.
coefficients.condition_fr: Le volume de la cuve par personne, en comptant la sciure ou les copeaux ajoutés à chaque passage.
coefficients.source: SSWM composting chamber factsheet and composting-toilet sizing practice
coefficients.notes: A SIZING figure: the Bases sheet marks per-person-per-year as not contributing to flow, so it is shown and never summed into anything. Stage 0 claimed 300 L flat; the sourced range runs to 500. | Condition as first written: CHAMBER capacity per person, INCLUDING the carbon bulking material added at each use, not the volume of excreta. Raw faeces alone are about 200 L/person/year and decompose to roughly a tenth of that; the chamber has to hold the material through its residence period plus the cover material. The low end matches industry sizing calculations, the high end the half-cubic-metre-per-person rule of thumb.

coefficients.condition: Water for the same amount of laundry as one machine load, which takes two to three buckets.
coefficients.condition_fr: L’eau pour la même quantité de linge qu’une machine, soit deux à trois seaux.
coefficients.source: Manual washing-device documentation and low-tech practice accounts
coefficients.notes: The result is worth reading twice: 20-75 L against an electric machine's sourced 48-54 L on the eco programme. **Hand washing is not clearly better on water once load size is normalised** -- it is better on ELECTRICITY, which is a different axis. A per-load comparison would have said the opposite. | Condition as first written: NORMALISED TO A MACHINE-EQUIVALENT LOAD, and that normalisation is the whole point. A bucket takes roughly 2-3 kg of laundry against a machine's 7-8 kg, so a raw per-load figure flatters hand washing about threefold. One plunger device quotes 6 L for the wash alone; a rinse roughly doubles it, giving 10-25 L per bucket load, times 2-3 buckets to do what one machine cycle does.

coefficients.condition: The exchanger's rated efficiency, a little below a ducted system's. Over a season it does a little less.
coefficients.condition_fr: Le rendement nominal de l’échangeur, un peu sous celui d’un système à gaines. Sur une saison, il fait un peu moins.
coefficients.source: Trade and manufacturer documentation for decentralised double-flow ventilation, with the lower bound from ADEME's range for heat-recovery ventilation generally
coefficients.notes: Sits beside the ducted MVHR's 0.70-0.90 so the renovation trade-off is visible: a decentralised unit gives up some recovery in exchange for needing no duct network, which is exactly why somebody chooses one. | Condition as first written: NOMINAL exchanger efficiency, not seasonal system efficiency -- the same distinction the ducted MVHR row carries. Ceramic-core decentralised units are quoted at up to 85 pc against more than 90 pc for a ducted system; the low end is ADEME's general floor for heat-recovery ventilation. Alternating-flow single-room units also depend on room pressure balance in a way a ducted system does not.

coefficients.condition: The share of the stream that is pushed up, about a tenth when it lifts six to ten times its fall. The higher the lift, the less; the rest flows on.
coefficients.condition_fr: La part du ruisseau qui est remontée, environ un dixième quand elle monte six à dix fois sa chute. Plus on monte haut, moins il en arrive ; le reste continue son cours.
coefficients.source: Peer-reviewed hydraulic ram pump studies and standard ram-pump design guidance
coefficients.notes: Keyed to the stream flow the reader supplies, because a ram pump's output is set by the stream, not by the pump. Flow is bucket-and-stopwatch measurable, which is what distinguishes this from wind: a site variable cheap enough to measure gets a coefficient, an expensive one gets a site prerequisite instead. | Condition as first written: VOLUMETRIC fraction of the drive flow delivered, not an energy efficiency. It falls as the lift rises: delivered over drive is roughly the D'Aubuisson efficiency times drive head over delivery head, and that efficiency runs 60-80 pc. The commonly quoted 'about 10 pc' assumes a lift of roughly six to ten times the drive head. The rest of the stream is not consumed, it runs on past the pump.

coefficients.condition: Area per person, for sink and shower water only, which is why it is smaller than for a system treating all wastewater. About 5 m² for a typical house.
coefficients.condition_fr: La surface par personne, pour les eaux d’évier et de douche seulement, d’où une surface plus petite que pour un système qui traite toutes les eaux usées. Environ 5 m² pour une maison courante.
coefficients.source: Arrete du 30 mars 2023 (five-year experimental authorisation for wood-chip filters treating greywater), with INRAE research behind it
coefficients.notes: A SIZING figure, never summed. Replaces nothing: this row previously carried no number at all. | Condition as first written: PER OCCUPANT AND FOR GREYWATER ONLY, which is NOT the same denominator as a person-equivalent. Greywater carries roughly 20 pc of the BOD5 of a full person-equivalent (and about 10 pc of the suspended solids), which is why this area is smaller than a system treating all wastewater. Do not compare it directly with the reed bed's 1.5-3 m2 per EH or the sand filter's 5 m2 per piece principale without accounting for that: those take the whole load. About 5 m2 total for a typical house.

coefficients.condition: The share of the warmth in the shower's drain water passed to the incoming cold water, fitted upright. The saving on the household's hot water is smaller, 10 to 27%.
coefficients.condition_fr: La part de la chaleur des eaux de douche transmise à l’eau froide qui arrive, en pose verticale. L’économie sur l’eau chaude du foyer est plus faible, 10 à 27 %.
coefficients.source: Peer-reviewed studies of vertical and horizontal drain-water heat exchangers
coefficients.notes: RECORDED, NOT SUMMED: it converts heat carried in a water stream, and the family model measures water in litres and heat in kWh. This is the same 'two quantities, one IO' limit as the water heaters. The figure is real and belongs on the solution page. MOVED FROM LOW-GRADE HEAT TO HOT WATER HEAT 2026-09-04. It pre-heats incoming cold water for a shower and never warmed a room; on the old io a space-heating demand could have drawn on it. | Condition as first written: EXCHANGER EFFECTIVENESS: the share of the heat in the draining water that is passed to the incoming cold feed, in a VERTICAL installation, varying with flow rate. This is NOT the household energy saving, which is 10-27 pc, because only shower water passes through it and only while the shower runs. Confusing the two overstates the benefit by roughly threefold.

coefficients.basis: per m2 of collector per year
coefficients.condition: Per m² of collector, for a system sized to its household in France: 500 kWh a year on average, 600 in the south. An oversized system wastes its summer surplus.
coefficients.condition_fr: Par m² de capteur, pour un système dimensionné pour son foyer en France : 500 kWh par an en moyenne, 600 dans le sud. Un système surdimensionné perd son surplus d’été.
coefficients.source: ADEME, fiche SOCOL 'La production d'eau chaude sanitaire a partir d'energie solaire dans les logements collectifs'
coefficients.notes: Written 2026-09-03 as a reference figure because Heated Water is a WATER io summed in litres and this is in kilowatt hours; moved onto Domestic hot water heat the same day, when that io and its family were created, and switched to Engine Use Y. Two further figures from the same ADEME fiche are recorded here because the schema has no home for them: a store sized at 50 litres per m2 of collector, and a design rule capping coverage at 80-90 pc in the best month, which is why productivity per m2 falls once a system is oversized. | Condition as first written: correctly-sized system, France; 500 kWh/m2/yr is the stated average, 350 the floor a sized system should not fall below, 600 reached in the south. Per m2 of CAPTEUR. Productivity is a property of the system as sized against its demand, not of the collector: the same source caps a good design at 80-90 pc coverage in the best month precisely because surplus beyond that is dumped

coefficients.condition: Per installation, not per person: the blower runs the same whether two people live there or six. Lower with an economy mode, higher with continuous air.
coefficients.condition_fr: Par installation, et non par personne : la soufflante tourne autant à deux qu’à six. Moins avec un mode éco, plus en aération continue.
coefficients.source: Manufacturer and installer figures for agreed French ANC units (ATB/PUROO quoting 30 kWh per rated EH per year; Bioxymop 483 +/- 87 kWh/yr for a 5 EH unit; trade sources putting the blower at 30-100 W continuous)
coefficients.notes: TIER C, AND IT SHOULD BE UPGRADED. The Tier A route exists: every agreed unit's fiche d'agrement publishes its consumption, and the ministry's ANC portal lists them. That portal returned 'service en cours de mise a jour' on 2026-09-03. A 3.5x spread is real and not a failure of sourcing: it is the gap between a throttled SBR and continuous aeration. Worth having because it is the honest counterweight to the micro-station's compactness -- a septic tank draws nothing. | Condition as first written: one domestic installation rated 5-6 EH, running year round. STATED PER INSTALLATION, NOT PER PERSON: the draw is the aeration blower's duty cycle, which is set by the unit's rated size and not by how many people live there, and the smallest units sold are 5-6 EH. A per-person basis would have under-counted a two-person household by more than half. Low end is a unit with an economy mode that throttles aeration under low load, high end continuous aeration

coefficients.condition: Efficiency over a standard day of hot-water use, counting the pilot, standby and reheating, which is why it is well below a burner's own efficiency.
coefficients.condition_fr: Le rendement sur une journée type de puisage, veilleuse, attente et réchauffage compris, d’où un chiffre bien inférieur à celui du brûleur seul.
coefficients.source: European Commission, Review Study on Water Heaters (2019), Task 5 market averages, as tabulated in the Topten/HACKS criteria paper D3.2 for water heaters; efficiency metric defined by Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 812/2013 and its minimum performance floor by Regulation (EU) 814/2013
coefficients.notes: THREE THINGS THE SOURCE SAYS ABOUT ITSELF, all of which widen rather than narrow this. (1) The values are catalogue-derived and the study warns of a bias toward products that bothered to declare, so the real market average is likely lower. (2) In practice the same paper puts gas instantaneous eta-wh anywhere from 10 pc (a pilot-light model) to 91 pc (condensing, Japan) -- the band here is European market average, not the full spread. (3) The published table is technology against ten load profiles and its column alignment did not survive PDF extraction for the two gas rows, so the band across all profiles is used rather than the value for one household size, which could not be read reliably. SECOND LIMIT, ours not theirs: this appliance accepts both mains gas and bottled gas, and a ratio may name only ONE input it converts from. The same efficiency applies to bottled gas; the row names mains gas because that is the row's commoner case and the engine needs a single answer. | Condition as first written: eta-wh, the regulated water-heating energy efficiency, on GROSS calorific value. Market-average values for gas-fired instantaneous water heaters on sale in 2018-19, spanning all load profiles. NOT a combustion efficiency: eta-wh is measured over a standard tapping pattern and already carries standby, pilot and reheat losses, which is why it sits well below a burner's 80-85 pc. The legal floor for any unit placed on the EU market at load profile M is 36 pc

coefficients.condition: Spare solar power sent to the water heater's element. The loss is the diverter's own use and the heat the tank gives off.
coefficients.condition_fr: Le surplus solaire envoyé à la résistance du chauffe-eau. La perte, c’est la consommation du routeur et la chaleur que dégage le ballon.
coefficients.source: Physical definition for the resistive element; standing loss regulated as parameter S in Commission Regulation (EU) No 814/2013. Diverter self-consumption from published device specifications
coefficients.notes: Deliberately slightly WORSE than the plain resistive cumulus (0.9-1.0), not better: a diverter adds electronics that draw power continuously and adds nothing thermally. It earns its place by using electricity that would otherwise be exported, which is a question about WHEN the energy is available and not about efficiency -- and this engine balances daily totals, so it cannot see that advantage at all. Read the verdict accordingly. | Condition as first written: surplus PV routed to a resistive immersion element. The element itself converts at 1.00 by definition; the band covers the diverter's own switching and standby draw plus the tank's standing loss, on the same reasoning and the same regulated standing-loss parameter as the resistive cumulus

coefficients.unit: kWh hot water / kWh flue gas
coefficients.condition: The share of the flue's heat the coil catches, only while the stove is lit: it thus follows the heating season, not your hot-water needs.
coefficients.condition_fr: La part de la chaleur des fumées que capte le serpentin, seulement quand le poêle est allumé : elle suit donc la saison de chauffe, pas vos besoins en eau chaude.
coefficients.source: EPA stove efficiency and flue-loss figures and a reclaimer's recovery share, as quoted by HY-C (chimney products manufacturer); recoverable flue-heat share corroborated independently by French practitioner sources
coefficients.notes: RESTATED 2026-09-04, and it is now summable. Written a day earlier as 0.05-0.11 per kWh of FUEL and excluded from the arithmetic, because a flue coil recovers from the stove's loss and the catalogue modelled only its delivered output, so there was no pool to draw from. Flue gas heat is now a stream in its own right, so the chain decomposes into the two figures it was always the product of: the stove loses 0.15-0.35 of its fuel up the flue, and a reclaimer captures 0.25-0.30 of that. TWO THINGS THE FIGURE CARRIES. The device measured is an air-to-air reclaimer with a fan and this row is a water thermosiphon coil: similar physics, different device, the same distance as the back-boiler figures already refused here. And the flue must stay hot enough -- creosote condenses below roughly 120 C, while the quoted device asks 177 C as its own margin, against typical flue gas of 149-343 C. WORTH KNOWING: at 10 kg of wood a day, about 40 kWh, this is 1.5-4.2 kWh/day against a two-person hot-water need of 3.06-3.56. Marginal, and seasonal. | Condition as first written: share of the heat in the flue gas that a reclaimer captures, on a stove that is already burning. Applies only while the stove runs, so the output follows the heating season and not the hot-water demand

coefficients.condition: A whole-house UV unit, for clear water. Cloudy or coloured rain or well water lets less light through, and the same lamp treats less.
coefficients.condition_fr: Un appareil UV pour toute la maison, pour une eau claire. Une eau de pluie ou de puits trouble ou colorée laisse passer moins de lumière, et la même lampe en traite moins.
coefficients.source: NSF/ANSI Class A and USEPA LT2ESWTR use 40 mJ/cm2 as the design dose; residential point-of-entry flow ratings from water-treatment industry buyer guides
coefficients.notes: TIER C BY PROVENANCE AND A DEVICE SPECIFICATION BY NATURE, which is the distinction section 1 of the quantification lessons asks to state on the row: a vendor quoting the flow its own lamp is certified for at a standardised dose is closer to a physical constant than to a performance claim, and the dose itself is set by NSF and the USEPA. WHY IT WAS WORTH WRITING: this is the benchmark option for water treatment and it was the only one of the three with no throughput, so the comparison was one-sided. Against the bio-sand filter's 60-180 L/h and the ceramic filter's 12-24 L/h, the conventional system is not marginally faster but one to two orders of magnitude faster -- and it needs mains pressure and continuous electricity to be so. That is the trade the catalogue exists to show. STILL MISSING on this row: the lamp's own electrical draw, which runs continuously and is the honest counterweight, on the same argument as the micro-station's blower. No sourced wattage was retrieved this pass. | Condition as first written: residential point-of-entry UV disinfection rated at 4-12 US gallons per minute, the range sold for whole-house use, AT A UV DOSE OF 40 mJ/cm2 AND 95 pc UV TRANSMITTANCE. Both conditions are load-bearing: the rated flow is not a property of the lamp alone but of lamp, dose and water clarity together, and turbidity or colour in rainwater or well water cuts transmittance and with it the flow the same lamp can treat. The UV step is taken as the system's limit because the sediment and carbon stages ahead of it are normally sized to pass more

coefficients.condition: The share of the wood's energy that goes up the flue. Set a little low on purpose, since some of the loss goes elsewhere (the casing, the ash).
coefficients.condition_fr: La part de l’énergie du bois qui part par le conduit. Fixée un peu basse exprès, car une partie de la perte part ailleurs (l’enveloppe, les cendres).
coefficients.source: EPA stove efficiency and flue-loss figures as quoted by HY-C (chimney products manufacturer)
coefficients.notes: The complement of the 0.65-0.80 already on this row from an independent source, which is corroboration rather than a duplicate: two passes months apart agree on the split. Written only for the two stoves that already carry a sourced efficiency. The rocket mass heater, rocket stove and TLUD get the OUTPUT so the waste is visible and linkable, and no figure -- they were refused an efficiency for want of a source that measures site-built stoves, and a loss figure would borrow the authority that refusal withheld. COMPLEMENTARY PAIR, AND THE HIGH CORNER IS NOT A REAL DEVICE. This row and the other ratio from the same input are two shares of one stream, but the sheet has no way to say so and the engine propagates low/low and high/high. So the high end here is paired with the high end there, which together would need more than the input provides. Every band in this tool is a bound rather than a joint distribution; the difference is that this corner is not merely unlikely, it is impossible. Read the high end as the ceiling of this share alone. Audited 2026-09-04. | Condition as first written: share of the fuel's energy leaving as hot flue gas. A certified stove runs at 65-80 pc efficiency and loses 20-35 pc, MOST OF WHICH goes up the flue but not all: casing losses, ash and unburnt fuel take a share nobody separates out. The low end is therefore set BELOW the measured total loss rather than equal to it, because routing the whole complement to the flue would overstate what a coil can recover, and optimistic is the direction this module refuses

coefficients.condition: The share of the wood's energy that goes up the flue. Set a little low on purpose, since some of the loss goes elsewhere (the casing, the ash).
coefficients.condition_fr: La part de l’énergie du bois qui part par le conduit. Fixée un peu basse exprès, car une partie de la perte part ailleurs (l’enveloppe, les cendres).
coefficients.source: EPA stove efficiency and flue-loss figures as quoted by HY-C (chimney products manufacturer)
coefficients.notes: The complement of the 0.65-0.80 already on this row from an independent source, which is corroboration rather than a duplicate: two passes months apart agree on the split. Written only for the two stoves that already carry a sourced efficiency. The rocket mass heater, rocket stove and TLUD get the OUTPUT so the waste is visible and linkable, and no figure -- they were refused an efficiency for want of a source that measures site-built stoves, and a loss figure would borrow the authority that refusal withheld. COMPLEMENTARY PAIR, AND THE HIGH CORNER IS NOT A REAL DEVICE. This row and the other ratio from the same input are two shares of one stream, but the sheet has no way to say so and the engine propagates low/low and high/high. So the high end here is paired with the high end there, which together would need more than the input provides. Every band in this tool is a bound rather than a joint distribution; the difference is that this corner is not merely unlikely, it is impossible. Read the high end as the ceiling of this share alone. Audited 2026-09-04. | Condition as first written: share of the fuel's energy leaving as hot flue gas. A certified stove runs at 65-80 pc efficiency and loses 20-35 pc, MOST OF WHICH goes up the flue but not all: casing losses, ash and unburnt fuel take a share nobody separates out. The low end is therefore set BELOW the measured total loss rather than equal to it, because routing the whole complement to the flue would overstate what a coil can recover, and optimistic is the direction this module refuses

coefficients.condition: The water sent to the drain with what was removed. Cold water, low pressure or a clogged membrane send more.
coefficients.condition_fr: L’eau envoyée à l’égout avec ce qui a été retiré. Une eau froide, une pression faible ou une membrane encrassée en envoient davantage.
coefficients.source: Complement of the sourced recovery ratio on the same solution
coefficients.notes: WRITTEN BECAUSE HIDING IT MISLED. The catalogue showed reverse osmosis producing potable water and nothing else, which omits the single most common criticism of the technique from a reader comparing it against a sand filter. It is the majority of the water put in. Derived from the recovery figure rather than sourced separately, so the two can never disagree. COMPLEMENTARY PAIR, AND THE HIGH CORNER IS NOT A REAL DEVICE. This row and the other ratio from the same input are two shares of one stream, but the sheet has no way to say so and the engine propagates low/low and high/high. So the high end here is paired with the high end there, which together would need more than the input provides. Every band in this tool is a bound rather than a joint distribution; the difference is that this corner is not merely unlikely, it is impossible. Read the high end as the ceiling of this share alone. Audited 2026-09-04. | Condition as first written: the complement of the recovery ratio already on this row: a domestic membrane delivers 20-50 pc of its feed as permeate and sends the rest to drain carrying the salts and contaminants removed. Recovery falls further with cold feed water, low pressure and a fouled membrane, so the reject share is a floor rather than a typical value

coefficients.condition: Fresh water topped up while the loop runs: from five litres a shower (the maker's figure) to thirty for ten minutes (measured).
coefficients.condition_fr: L’eau fraîche ajoutée pendant que la boucle tourne : de cinq litres par douche (chiffre du fabricant) à trente pour dix minutes (mesuré).
coefficients.source: Manufacturer claims for closed-loop shower systems, reported and measured in technology press coverage
coefficients.notes: A SIX-FOLD SPREAD INSIDE ONE SOURCE SET, kept rather than resolved. The likeliest explanation is that five litres is the initial charge and thirty is everything that passes through including top-ups, but nothing states which, and choosing would mean picking between a marketing number and a journalist's measurement without telling the reader. The band's width is the honest report of that. NOT WRITTEN: the unit's electricity. The only figure available, 0.80 kWh for a ten-minute shower, is dominated by heating the water rather than by the pump and the UV lamp -- 30 litres raised 30 K is 1.05 kWh by itself -- and nothing separates the two. | Condition as first written: fresh water drawn while the loop runs, which is a top-up rather than the flow at the head: the water crossing the showerhead is mostly the same water going round again. The low end is the manufacturer's 'five litres however long you shower', the high end a measured ten-minute run reported at 30 litres. Against 6-12 L/min for a conventional shower on the same basis

coefficients.condition: What comes back as electricity for what went in, for a home-sized system around 200 bar. Better figures exist only in laboratories.
coefficients.condition_fr: Ce qui revient en électricité pour ce qui est entré, pour un système domestique vers 200 bars. De meilleurs chiffres n’existent qu’en laboratoire.
coefficients.source: Low-tech Magazine, 'Ditch the Batteries: Off-Grid Compressed Air Energy Storage', summarising the research literature it cites
coefficients.notes: THE FIGURE MOST LIKELY TO BE QUOTED WRONGLY. The same article gives 'close to 70 pc' for a home-scale high-pressure system, and that is an EXERGETIC efficiency which counts the recovered heat -- hot water from compression, cold from expansion -- as useful output. The ELECTRICITY returned is 11-17 pc. Using 70 here would overstate what the electricity family can draw by four to six times, and 70 is the number a reader attracted to 'ditch the batteries' meets first. WORTH KNOWING, and it is the point of having the figure: against a lead-acid bank at 0.70-0.85 and lithium at 0.92-0.98, compressed air gives back roughly a sixth of what it is given. Its case is service life, simplicity and no chemistry to replace, and this row is what that case costs. The exergetic figure is real and is not nothing -- it means the losses come back as heat you can use -- but heat is not electricity and this family is measured in electricity. | Condition as first written: ELECTRIC-TO-ELECTRIC round trip for a home-scale high-pressure system, around 200 bar, with the heat of compression not recovered. Laboratory low-pressure designs at 3-8 bar reach 60-85 pc, but those are research prototypes with liquid pistons or modular cylinder arrays rather than something a reader can build

coefficients.condition: What one household unit treats a day, running all the time (the smallest about 190 litres). Anything beyond goes where untreated greywater went before.
coefficients.condition_fr: Ce qu’une unité domestique traite par jour en continu (la plus petite environ 190 litres). Le reste part là où partaient les eaux grises non traitées.
coefficients.source: Manufacturer specifications for domestic greywater recycling package units, corroborated across several suppliers
coefficients.notes: A MID-CHAIN CAP, which is the kind of figure that now earns its keep: when the unit is the binding step the panel says so by name, and a reader learns that a bigger greywater supply will not give them more reclaimed water. RECORDED BUT NOT SUMMED, because there is no basis for it: an MBR uses 0.5-1.5 kWh per cubic metre treated in most reports, one packaged system 1.26, and one study 3.3. Over half of that is aeration, for microbial growth and to keep the membrane from fouling. Expressing it per day would tangle the unit's SIZE with its energy INTENSITY, which are two different things and would move together wrongly. Worth having when a per-volume basis exists. | Condition as first written: rated throughput of a packaged single-household unit, running continuously. Commercial units are sold in steps rather than sized freely: roughly 190 L/day at the smallest, then 300, then 1000 and up. A household treating more than the unit is rated for does not get more treated water, it gets the overflow sent wherever untreated greywater was going before

coefficients.condition: A small petrol or diesel set. A backup set usually runs well below its rated power, where it wastes more fuel.
coefficients.condition_fr: Un petit groupe essence ou diesel. Un groupe de secours tourne souvent bien sous sa puissance, là où il gaspille le plus de carburant.
coefficients.source: Generator trade and supplier technical guides for specific fuel consumption, converted using standard net calorific values
coefficients.notes: WRITTEN ONLY AFTER ERIC PINNED THE FUEL (2026-09-04). While this row's input was the generic Biomass Fuel there was no honest figure to give: a petrol genset and a wood-gas one are different machines with different numbers, and picking one would have answered a catalogue question silently. A CONTRADICTION INSIDE THE SOURCES, resolved rather than averaged. Several trade pages quote 'fuel efficiency ratings' of 50-60 pc for petrol and 58-65 pc for diesel. Those cannot be electrical conversion efficiencies -- the same pages state 0.4 L/kWh, which works out at 25 pc, and no small genset approaches 60. The physical route, specific consumption against calorific value, is used instead and the marketing figure is ignored. WORTH KNOWING: at 0.20-0.32 a generator turns roughly a quarter of its fuel into electricity, so a kWh from a can of petrol costs about four kWh of fuel. That is the number that makes a battery worth having, and it is why this row is a BACKUP. | Condition as first written: small portable or standby set, petrol or diesel. DERIVED from published specific consumption of 0.30-0.45 litres per kWh against net calorific values of 9.6 kWh/L for petrol and 10.7 for diesel. Large stationary diesels reach 40 pc and above; this row is not one of those, and a backup set is usually LIGHTLY LOADED, where efficiency falls further -- peak efficiency is around 75-80 pc of rated output

coefficients.unit: kW per (m3/s x m of head)
coefficients.basis: per m3/s per metre of head
coefficients.condition: From the stream to the wire, counting the turbine, drive and generator, and the height lost in the pipe. A narrow pipe loses much more.
coefficients.condition_fr: Du ruisseau au câble, en comptant turbine, transmission et générateur, et la hauteur perdue dans la conduite. Une conduite trop étroite en perd beaucoup plus.
coefficients.source: Renewables First (hydropower developer) component efficiencies and the standard P = head x flow x 9.81 formulation; energypedia hydro power basics
coefficients.notes: THE FIRST ROW ON A BASIS THAT NEEDED TWO SCALE INPUTS, and the basis had been sitting in the sheet unimplemented: the menu offered flow and head, the engine had no case for them, and any row written against it would have vanished as missing-scenario. Found by broadening the basis check from 'every basis in use' to 'every basis declared'. A STREAM RUNS DAY AND NIGHT, which is the honest part of micro-hydro's appeal: unlike PV it has no worst month from darkness. It has one from DROUGHT, and this engine does not model that -- the flow entered is treated as the flow all year. A reader on a seasonal stream should enter the SUMMER low flow, not the annual average, and that instruction matters more than the coefficient does. The gross-versus-net head trap is the denominator error waiting on this row: quoting a system efficiency against gross head, as most casual guides do, overstates output by 10-20 pc before anything else goes wrong. | Condition as first written: the whole chain from the stream to the wire, so the figure already carries gravity (9.81) and every efficiency between. Two things are folded in and both matter. SYSTEM efficiency: a well-built small scheme runs turbine 85 pc x drive 95 pc x generator 93 pc, about 75 pc overall, and 50 pc is the conservative figure practical guides use. GROSS-TO-NET HEAD: the standard formula wants NET head, and a reader measures the vertical drop, which is GROSS. Penstock friction costs roughly 10-20 pc of it in a well-sized pipe and much more in an undersized one, so 0.75 x 0.90 gives the top of this range and 0.50 x 0.80 the bottom

coefficients.condition: Trench length per main room, from good soil to poor soil (French rule DTU 64.1). Each trench at most 30 m, and 1.5 m apart.
coefficients.condition_fr: La longueur de tranchée par pièce principale, d’un bon sol à un sol médiocre (DTU 64.1). Chaque tranchée fait au plus 30 m, à 1,5 m l’une de l’autre.
coefficients.source: NF DTU 64.1 (assainissement non collectif), as tabulated by French ANC technical guidance and public-sector fiches
coefficients.notes: A SIZING FIGURE, so the Bases sheet keeps it out of the arithmetic entirely: metres of trench cannot be added to litres per day. It is shown and never summed, like the reed beds and the sand filter. WHY IT IS A RANGE AND NOT A RATE, which is the same objection that kept the septic TANK volume out of this sheet: the rule is stepped and doubly conditioned. Per room it works out at 9 m in good soil and 16 in poor, and the marginal room costs 6 m rather than 9, so no single rate describes it. The range brackets the table; the table is in the condition. AND THE CONDITIONING VARIABLE IS MEASURABLE BY THE READER, which is why this is recorded at all rather than refused outright: soil permeability comes from a percolation test, which is a morning's work with a bucket and a watch. It is the same reasoning that let stream flow earn a coefficient where wind speed did not. | Condition as first written: total length of infiltration trench, per piece principale, which French ANC practice counts as one person-equivalent. THE PUBLISHED RULE IS A STEPPED TABLE, NOT A RATE, and this range is its span rather than a coefficient: DTU 64.1 sets 45 m for five rooms in good soil (permeability above 50 mm/h) plus 6 m per extra room, 50 m plus 10 for medium soil, and 80 m plus 16 for poor soil (15-30 mm/h). Trench length is capped at 30 m each and they sit at least 1.5 m apart

coefficients.condition: A whole home lit with LEDs, per home, not per person: lighting follows the number of rooms, not of people. About 110 kWh a year (ADEME).
coefficients.condition_fr: Un logement entier éclairé en LED, par logement et non par personne : l’éclairage suit le nombre de pièces, pas d’occupants. Environ 110 kWh par an (ADEME).
coefficients.source: ADEME ElecDom measured consumption panel, reported through French energy-sector guides
coefficients.notes: THE SECOND ROW ON THIS SOLUTION, and the two are not alternatives. The existing figure is luminous efficacy in lumens per watt, which describes the LAMP and cannot be summed into an electricity total; this one describes the HOUSEHOLD and can. They share a solution and nothing else, which is why they carry different bases. FOUND BY MEASURING COVERAGE rather than by looking for a figure: a realistic whole-house graph had figures for only 11 of its 29 flow-carrying solutions, and lighting -- one of the most universal electrical loads there is -- turned out to have no demand at all. WORTH KNOWING: 80-150 kWh a year is under 3 pc of a French household's electricity, and the same lighting on halogen would be 550 and on incandescent 660. The saving is real and already banked; lighting is no longer where a reader should look for one. | Condition as first written: a whole household lit with LEDs, PER DWELLING and not per person: lighting scales with the number of rooms and fittings rather than with occupancy, so a couple in a large house lights more than a family in a flat. ADEME's ElecDom measured panel (July 2023 to July 2024) puts it at 110 kWh a year and ADEME elsewhere quotes 147; a worked example of ten LED sources at three hours a day gives 80, and a 31-point house about 105

coefficients.condition: Losses in the cables at full load, within the limits of the French wiring standard. Most of the time a circuit carries less and loses less.
coefficients.condition_fr: Les pertes dans les câbles à pleine charge, dans les limites de la NF C 15-100. La plupart du temps, un circuit porte moins et perd moins.
coefficients.source: NF C 15-100 voltage-drop limits for domestic installations (equivalently IEC 60364)
coefficients.notes: WRITTEN INSTEAD OF FLAGGING THIS ROW AS A CONDUIT. It was a candidate: electricity in, electricity out, no transformation. But Eric's test for a conduit is that there is no MEASURABLE loss, and cable loss is not only measurable, it is capped by regulation, which makes it one of the easier figures in this sheet to defend. A pipe with a known leak is not a pipe. SMALL AND WORTH HAVING ANYWAY: at 0.95-0.99 it will rarely move a verdict, but it is the honest floor under every electrical chain, and leaving it out would have meant claiming a distribution board is lossless. | Condition as first written: cable loss across a domestic distribution board and its final circuits, AT FULL LOAD. NF C 15-100 caps voltage drop at 3 pc for lighting circuits and 5 pc for others, and for a largely resistive domestic load the power lost is close to the voltage dropped. The real figure sits nearer the top of this range most of the time, because a circuit is rarely at its design current and the drop falls with it

coefficients.unit: kWh per kg seasoned / kWh per kg green
coefficients.condition: Heat from a kilogram of dry wood compared with green wood: dry wood gives nearly twice as much.
coefficients.condition_fr: La chaleur d’un kilo de bois sec comparé à du bois vert : le bois sec en donne près de deux fois plus.
coefficients.source: ADEME and French wood-fuel technical guidance on calorific value against moisture content; the 20 pc figure is the same one already carried on the Biomass Fuel resource
coefficients.notes: ENGINE USE N, AND THE REASON IS THAT IT WOULD DOUBLE-COUNT. The Biomass Fuel resource already states its energy density AT 20 PC MOISTURE, so the fuel a reader enters is already assumed seasoned. Applying this ratio on top would grant the seasoning gain twice. IT IS WRITTEN BECAUSE IT IS THE REASON THE STORE EXISTS. A woodshed is not storage in the sense a cistern is: it performs a transformation, and it is what makes the catalogue's own 3.8-4.2 kWh/kg true. Skip it and a reader loses close to half the heat in their woodpile. THIS ROW IS ALSO WHY FIREWOOD STORAGE FAILED THE CONDUIT TEST on 2026-09-04: fuel in, fuel out, and a measurable change in between. Around 1000 kg of green wood becomes about 625 kg at 20 pc, and every one of those kilograms is worth nearly twice as much. | Condition as first written: usable heat from a kilogram of correctly seasoned wood against a kilogram of green wood. Wood at 20 pc moisture gives 3.8-4.2 kWh/kg and at 50 pc about 2.2-2.5, because the heat that would have reached the room is spent boiling off the water instead. Burning green wood therefore takes close to twice the mass for the same heat

coefficients.condition: A year's use, running every two to three days.
coefficients.condition_fr: Sur une année, à raison d’un cycle tous les deux ou trois jours.
coefficients.source: Manufacturer and comparison-site figures for countertop electric composters (FoodCycler, Lomi, Reencle), cross-checked against their advertised running cost
coefficients.notes: THE POINT OF HAVING IT is the comparison it makes possible: a compost heap uses nothing, and this is the benchmark option beside it. **The convenience costs about as much electricity as lighting the whole house** (80-150 kWh/yr on the LED row). ONE DISTINCTION THE SOURCES MAKE AND THE ROW CANNOT: most of these machines DEHYDRATE rather than compost, shrinking waste into dry matter that still needs composting afterwards, while a few genuinely decompose it. They are not the same appliance and the catalogue has one row for both. Worth splitting if the row ever carries a claim about the OUTPUT rather than about the electricity. | Condition as first written: a countertop electric composter run every two to three days. Reported consumption is 0.5-1.5 kWh a cycle, with a dehydrating unit around 0.8-1; at three cycles a week that is roughly 80-230 kWh a year, and the running cost these units are advertised at, about two dollars a month, independently implies around 150. STATED PER YEAR ON PURPOSE: the per-cycle basis in this sheet carries a LAUNDRY frequency, and a composter borrowing it would inherit a washing machine's rhythm

coefficients.condition: Water for the same amount of laundry as one machine load, which takes three to four pedal-drum loads.
coefficients.condition_fr: L’eau pour la même quantité de linge qu’une machine, soit trois à quatre tambours à pédale.
coefficients.source: Manufacturer figures for foot-pedal drum washers and DIY build guides, normalised against the EU standard load
coefficients.notes: THE COMPARISON IS THE POINT, and it does not go the way the hand-washing one did. Against an electric machine's 48-54 L on the eco programme and a bucket's 20-75, a pedal drum at 15-38 is **the best of the three on water AND uses no electricity**. Hand washing, on the same normalisation, was only better on electricity. WITHOUT THE NORMALISATION THIS WOULD HAVE BEEN A REAL ERROR RATHER THAN A ROSY ONE. The per-cycle basis multiplies by 0.5-0.7 MACHINE loads a day. A 2 kg drum entered at its raw 10 litres would have been credited with washing a 7.5 kg household load for 10 litres, understating its water by roughly a factor of four. Third technology in this catalogue to meet the laundry load-size trap. | Condition as first written: NORMALISED TO A MACHINE-EQUIVALENT LOAD, following the same convention as the bucket washer, because without it this row would be wrong in the arithmetic and not merely flattering. A pedal drum holds about 2-2.5 kg of dry laundry against a machine's 7-8, and the frequency this basis carries is the EU reference of 220 MACHINE cycles a year. Raw figures are 5 litres to wash and 5 to rinse on a commercial foot-pedal unit, and 5-10 litres a load on DIY builds; multiplied by the three to four loads that make one machine load, that is 15-38

coefficients.condition: A dish left connected: it is always on. More in rain and snow, when it heats itself to stay clear.
coefficients.condition_fr: Une antenne laissée branchée : elle ne s’éteint jamais. Davantage sous la pluie et la neige, quand elle se chauffe pour rester dégagée.
coefficients.source: Manufacturer specifications and off-grid power guides for the standard Starlink terminal, cross-checked across several independent measurements
coefficients.notes: WRITTEN BECAUSE IT IS AN OFF-GRID DECISION, not a gadget. Against the everyday connectivity rows already in the same sub-function at 150-300 kWh/yr, a satellite terminal is roughly **twice** the load, and on a 3 kWp array it is a material share of the year's generation. For a rural site with no fixed line it may be the only option, which is exactly why its cost should be visible rather than assumed away. THE SEASONAL SHAPE IS THE PART AN ANNUAL FIGURE HIDES, and it runs the wrong way: the dish draws MOST in the cold and wet, which is when a PV array generates LEAST. This engine reports the worse of annual and worst month, but it has no monthly profile for a constant load, so the worst month here is understated. Said on the row because nothing in the arithmetic will say it. | Condition as first written: a standard dish left connected. It draws 50-75 W in use and about 20 W idle, and reported real-world averages are 1-1.5 kWh a day. THERE IS NO STANDBY WORTH THE NAME: the terminal is always on, which is what separates it from a router. Consumption rises in rain and snow because the dish heats itself to stay clear, so a Normandy winter sits above the annual average this figure states

coefficients.condition: On the eco programme, for 13 place settings.
coefficients.condition_fr: Sur le programme éco, pour 13 couverts.
coefficients.source: EU energy label declared values for 13-place-setting dishwashers on the eco programme, measured under Commission Regulation (EU) 2019/2022
coefficients.notes: The same regulatory shape as the washing machine row, and the eco programme is the one the label is measured on rather than the one most people press. | Condition as first written: eco programme, 13 place settings, the mandated test cycle. Declared values for current machines cluster tightly: 9.0 and 9.9 litres on two models from different makers

coefficients.condition: On the eco programme, for 13 place settings. Most of it heats the water, which is why that programme is slow.
coefficients.condition_fr: Sur le programme éco, pour 13 couverts. L’essentiel chauffe l’eau, d’où la lenteur de ce programme.
coefficients.source: EU energy label declared values for 13-place-setting dishwashers on the eco programme, measured under Commission Regulation (EU) 2019/2022
coefficients.notes: Worth reading beside the hand-washing row, which draws no electricity but asks the household to heat several times the water by some other means. The comparison is only fair if that heat is counted, and this catalogue counts it in the hot-water family. | Condition as first written: eco programme, 13 place settings. Declared values of 0.736 and 0.936 kWh on two current models. MOST OF THIS IS HEATING THE WATER, not driving the pump, which is why the eco programme is slow: it washes longer at a lower temperature

coefficients.condition: Water for a dishwasher's load washed by hand in two filled basins. A running tap uses far more.
coefficients.condition_fr: L’eau pour une charge de lave-vaisselle lavée à la main dans deux bacs remplis. Au robinet qui coule, on en use bien plus.
coefficients.source: University of Bonn dishwashing research (Stamminger and Schencking), as reported by consumer testing organisations
coefficients.notes: THE RESULT IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE LAUNDRY ONE AND SHOULD BE READ AS SUCH. Normalising load size took the shine off hand washing clothes; here it removes it entirely. Even the best measured hand method uses roughly three to six times a machine's 9-10 litres, and the machine also heats its own water rather than asking the household to. THE BAND IS WIDE BECAUSE THE METHOD IS A HABIT, not a device. Nothing about two basins enforces two basins, and the study's 33-to-440 spread is almost entirely whether the tap was left running. | Condition as first written: NORMALISED TO A MACHINE-EQUIVALENT LOAD, the same convention as the bucket and pedal washing machines, so the two rows in this sub-function can be read against each other. The Bonn research cleans 144 items in a full machine and finds hand washing the same load averages about 100 litres, from 33 at best to 440 at worst. This range is the FILLED-BASIN method specifically, which is where the low end of that spread comes from; a running tap belongs at the other end and is not what this row describes

coefficients.condition: One shower a day: 2 to 5 litres for the whole shower, since the tank sets how much is used.
coefficients.condition_fr: Une douche par jour : 2 à 5 litres pour toute la douche, puisque c’est le réservoir qui fixe la quantité.
coefficients.source: Low-tech Lab wiki, Biosphere Urbaine : La douche econome en eau et en energie
coefficients.notes: READ THIS AGAINST SOL-091 AND SOL-092, which carry 60-80 L/person/day on the same basis: that is the factor-of-ten claim the experiment was built to test, and it held. The tier is C because it is one installation reporting on itself, not a standard. NOT expressed per minute of showering, unlike the other three showers in this sub-function, and that is deliberate: multiplying a per-minute figure by the usual 5-12 minute band would not reproduce 2-5 litres, since this shower ends when the tank does. | Condition as first written: One shower a day, measured over the four-month experiment: 2 to 5 litres for a whole shower rather than per minute, because a misting shower's water use is bounded by its tank and not by how long the user stands there

coefficients.basis: per m2 of fog net per foggy day
coefficients.condition: Measured where fog is frequent (Morocco, Chile, the Canaries…). A test net must give more than 5 litres per m² before a project starts.
coefficients.condition_fr: Mesuré là où le brouillard est fréquent (Maroc, Chili, Canaries…). Un filet d’essai doit donner plus de 5 litres par m² avant de lancer un projet.
coefficients.source: Munich Re Foundation, "IntoAction 5: Fog nets" (32 pp.), citing Correggiari et al.
coefficients.notes: NOT USED BY THE ENGINE, on purpose. Every one of these numbers comes from a fog belt, and this row's own description says Normandy is nowhere near that frequency and has no site data. Feeding it in would credit a reader with water the site may never deliver, and the tool would contradict the sentence directly above it. It is here as an order of magnitude and as the 5 L/m2 threshold a reader can test their own site against. | Condition as first written: Measured across operating installations in fog belts: Morocco, Chile, Eritrea, Oman, Peru, the Canaries, Nepal and South Africa. The best sites exceed 30 L/m2/day at peak, and the programme's own go/no-go rule is that a test net must return more than 5 L/m2 before a project is planned at all

coefficients.condition: From the legal minimum for a pellet stove on sale to the best on the market. A home-built stove comes with no such guarantee.
coefficients.condition_fr: Du minimum légal pour un poêle à granulés vendu dans le commerce au meilleur du marché. Un poêle fait maison n’offre pas cette garantie.
coefficients.source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2015/1185 (ecodesign, solid fuel local space heaters), Annexes II and V
coefficients.notes: C10, 2026-10-30. Annex II read: 79 pc minimum for closed fronted pellet heaters. Annex V benchmark 94 pc seen in a search excerpt of the same regulation. Applies to appliances placed on the market, not to a gravity-fed self-build.

coefficients.condition: From the legal minimum for a solid-fuel cooker on sale to the best on the market.
coefficients.condition_fr: Du minimum légal pour une cuisinière à combustible solide vendue dans le commerce au meilleur du marché.
coefficients.source: Commission Regulation (EU) 2015/1185 (ecodesign, solid fuel local space heaters), Annexes II and V
coefficients.notes: C10, 2026-10-30. Annex II read: 65 pc for cookers. Annex V benchmark 75 pc seen in a search excerpt of the same regulation.

coefficients.condition: About how much of the electricity reaches the pan. One published figure, so no range.
coefficients.condition_fr: À peu près la part de l’électricité qui arrive dans la casserole. Un seul chiffre publié, donc pas de fourchette.
coefficients.source: ENERGY STAR, Residential Induction Cooking Tops (2021 Emerging Technology Award)
coefficients.notes: C10, 2026-10-30. Read: "approximately 85% efficiency". A US programme; a single approximate figure.

coefficients.condition: About how much of the gas’s energy reaches the pan. One published figure, so no range.
coefficients.condition_fr: À peu près la part de l’énergie du gaz qui arrive dans la casserole. Un seul chiffre publié, donc pas de fourchette.
coefficients.source: ENERGY STAR, Residential Induction Cooking Tops (2021 Emerging Technology Award)
coefficients.notes: C10, 2026-10-30. Read: "approximately 32%". A US programme; a single approximate figure.

coefficients.condition: Lab runs at high power, with a pot skirt and a light stove top: a tuned best case, so expect less at home.
coefficients.condition_fr: Essais en laboratoire à forte puissance, avec une jupe de casserole et un dessus léger : un cas optimisé, à attendre moindre chez soi.
coefficients.source: Aprovecho Research Center, Mass, Insulation and Thermal Efficiency
coefficients.notes: C10, 2026-10-30. Read: 46.1 to 51.7 pc across four runs. The stoves’ own developer; names no test protocol.

coefficients.condition: An hour of moderate pedalling a day, at 45 to 75 W of electricity. Pedal for longer and it scales.
coefficients.condition_fr: Une heure de pédalage modéré par jour, à 45-75 W d’électricité. Plus longtemps, c’est proportionnel.
coefficients.source: Low-tech Magazine, How to Build a Practical Household Bike Generator (2022)
coefficients.notes: C10, 2026-10-30. Read: 45-75 W at moderate effort. The hour a day is our assumption, not the source’s.

coefficients.condition: An hour of hand pumping a day: 35 litres a minute from 10 m down, 10 litres a minute from 35 m.
coefficients.condition_fr: Une heure de pompage à la main par jour : 35 litres par minute à 10 m de profondeur, 10 litres par minute à 35 m.
coefficients.source: PRACTICA Foundation, Rope Pump technical training handbook (2011)
coefficients.notes: C10, 2026-10-30. Read: 35 l/min at 10 m, 20 at 20 m, 10 at 35 m. The hour a day is our assumption, not the source’s.

coefficients.condition: All of the flow you measure at the spring. Measure it at the end of the dry season, the least you can count on.
coefficients.condition_fr: Tout le débit que vous mesurez à la source. À mesurer en fin de saison sèche, le minimum sur lequel compter.
coefficients.source: Oxfam, Spring protection technical brief (2008)
coefficients.notes: C10, 2026-10-30. NOT A MEASURED FIGURE: 1.0 means the reader’s own flow is the supply. Oxfam’s dry-season advice seen in a search excerpt, not read in full.

coefficients.condition: A 1 kW turbine, from a rooftop (4.2% of its rated power on average) to a free-standing mast (19%), in UK field trials. Your site’s wind decides where you fall.
coefficients.condition_fr: Une éolienne de 1 kW, du toit (4,2 % de sa puissance nominale en moyenne) au mât isolé (19 %), d’après des essais au Royaume-Uni. Le vent de votre terrain décide où vous vous situez.
coefficients.source: Drew et al., Renewable Energy (2015), citing the Warwick wind trials and the Energy Saving Trust field trial
coefficients.notes: C10, 2026-10-30. Paper read; the trials themselves only through it. Load factor x 8760 h is our calculation. Fixed at 1 kW until the check has a turbine size setting.

coefficients.condition: What comes back out for what went in, over a full charge and discharge, for lead-acid batteries. The same as a smaller bank: only the size differs.
coefficients.condition_fr: Ce qui ressort pour ce qui est entré, sur une charge et une décharge complètes, pour des batteries au plomb. Comme un parc plus petit : seule la taille change.
coefficients.source: As Battery bank (SOL-080)
coefficients.notes: C10, 2026-10-30. Same technology as SOL-080, only larger.

fabric_classes.condition: space-heating BESOIN -- the heat the building needs delivered into its rooms, before any heating system's efficiency. Interquartile range (p25-p75) of diagnosed INDIVIDUAL HOUSES carrying label A in climate zone H1a; the median is 48. Half of real houses with this label fall inside the band. Flats are excluded: a shared wall has a heated neighbour behind it and a different surface-to-volume ratio, which is not a fact about the reader's own envelope
fabric_classes.source: ADEME, base des diagnostics de performance energetique des logements existants (depuis juillet 2021), champ besoin_chauffage rapporte a surface_habitable_logement, maisons individuelles
fabric_classes.notes: SAMPLED, NOT EXHAUSTIVE: 1999 records read from a dataset of about 15.5 million, and the API returns an ORDERED SLICE rather than a random sample. Measured, that bias is real: an unfiltered slice ran 41 pc H1a against a true 36 pc. It is handled here by STRATIFYING on the climate zone, which is the variable this figure is about; within a zone the department mix is still uneven, so read this band as characteristic of the zone rather than as an exact quantile of it. WHY THE LETTER AND NOT THE DPE NUMBER: the DPE headline figure is PRIMARY energy across five uses and would double-count the hot water this catalogue already models on IO-41. This column is the separate besoin field from the same record, which needs no conversion.

departments._what: Each metropolitan French department, its region, and the RE2020 climate zone its own DPE diagnostics carry.
departments._method: Zone derived from ADEME's DPE database, one query per department, taking the zone the department's diagnostics actually record. Names and regions from geo.api.gouv.fr.
departments._confidence: Least unanimous department: Vaucluse (H2d) at 97.3% agreement across 116099 diagnostics.
departments._not_checked: That the reference weather point chosen for each zone is the OFFICIAL station, or is representative of the whole zone. That each point at least sits INSIDE its own zone is checked, by check_reference_points below -- it caught H1a and H1b transposed. Representativeness is a different and harder question: H1a runs from the Channel coast to the Paris basin, and Trappes speaks for all of it.

climate.framework: RE2020 / CEE eight-zone split (H1a-c, H2a-d, H3), approved by the arrete du 4 aout 2021. Adopted rather than invented: ADEME already publishes solar-thermal yield by these zones, so our figures line up with an existing source.
climate.reference_period: 1991-2020 for normals; 1991-2024 for the interannual series

tracc._what: Trajectoire de rechauffement de reference pour l'adaptation au changement climatique, the French national adaptation reference trajectory, carried into the third PNACC (March 2025).
tracc._scope_limit: Apply to TEMPERATURE-driven figures only. The precipitation signal is weak: the two models behind the French projections sit in the lower range of the European multi-model ensemble for extreme precipitation. Do NOT shift a rainwater coefficient by a projected rainfall delta; state the projected change with its uncertainty instead.

pv.condition: 14% system loss, optimal angles (slope 38 deg, azimuth -4)

degree_days.basis: Daily mean 2m air temperature. Heating degree-days on base 18 C, the French DJU convention. 'hot_days' counts days whose MEAN reaches the threshold, which is a measure of exposure and not a cooling demand: a cooling demand would need a building.

rain_interannual.source: NASA POWER monthly (MERRA-2), aggregated to annual totals
rain_interannual._note: p10 is the typical dry year; driest is the worst in the record. They give different verdicts on the same chain, so the adequacy module must expose which basis it used.

pv.condition: 14% system loss, optimal angles (slope 37 deg, azimuth -1)

_checked_since: WHICH ZONE A DEPARTMENT IS IN. Derived 2026-09-05 from ADEME's DPE database by build_departments.py, one query per department, taking the zone that department's own diagnostics record. All 96 metropolitan departments resolved; the least unanimous was Vaucluse at 97.3 pc across 116,099 diagnostics. This used to sit in _not_checked and no longer does.
climate._WARNING: Reference POINTS are unconfirmed: the coordinates below are approximate town centres, not the official RE2020 stations. The zone a department belongs to IS now confirmed (see _checked_since), so the earlier blanket instruction not to ship a zone selector has been narrowed rather than ignored: a selector may ship PROVIDED the interface names the town whose climate it is using, so the reader knows they are getting Nancy or Agen rather than an official zone average. Do not present these as the arrete's own reference figures until climate-zones.json says zone_table_confirmed: true.
